w:r.w:t: EmPay is a lightweight, full-stack Human Resource and Payroll Management System (HRMS) designed for Indian startups, SMEs, and institutions with 10–200 employees. It solves three critical pain points: fragmented HR tooling, manual payroll compliance, and zero employee self-service.

Built as a 24-hour hackathon prototype by a 2-engineer team, EmPay demonstrates the complete data flow from employee onboarding through attendance tracking, leave management, payroll computation, and analytics — all in a single integrated platform.
Indian SMEs, startups, educational institutions (10–200 employees)
Lighter than Keka/Darwinbox, more powerful than Kredily, open-source

The global HRMS market is valued at $30.86B in 2025 and projected to reach $89.12B by 2035 (CAGR 11.19%). India is the fastest-growing segment, with 67% of Indian companies now using payroll software and HR tech ranking as the #1 software investment priority for Indian enterprises in 2025.
Most Indian SMEs manage payroll in Excel. As teams grow past 20 employees, manual tracking leads to recurring errors, compliance risks, and HR bandwidth drain.

India's 4 New Labour Codes (effective Nov 2025) and the new Income Tax Act (Apr 2026) represent the most significant payroll reform in decades. Existing off-the-shelf tools lag behind. Manual compliance is the #1 SME pain point.
Attendance, leave, and payroll are tracked in disconnected tools. A leave approval does not automatically affect payrun computation — creating costly reconciliation overhead.

Employees query HR for every payslip, leave balance, or attendance record. This consumes significant HR time that should be spent on strategic work. 68% of Indian employees use mobile apps for HR tasks but have no ESS portal.
Deliver a unified HRMS that covers the complete Employee → Attendance → Leave → Payroll → Analytics lifecycle in one platform.
Automate Indian payroll compliance: PF (12%), Professional Tax (Maharashtra slabs), ESIC, and LOP deduction.
Enforce granular Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) with 4 distinct roles: Admin, HR Officer, Payroll Officer, and Employee.
Provide an Employee Self-Service portal so employees can independently manage attendance, leave, and payslips.
Generate PDF payslips with compliant salary breakdown for each employee per payrun.

System shall authenticate users via email + password with bcrypt verification
System shall issue a signed JWT (HS256) containing user ID, email, and role on successful login
JWT shall expire in 8 hours; expired tokens must return HTTP 401
Role embedded in JWT shall be verified in middleware on every protected API route
Frontend ProtectedRoute HOC shall redirect unauthorized roles to /unauthorized
HR Officer and Admin can create employee profiles with: name, email, department, designation, joining date, employment type
Admin can configure annual CTC per employee; system auto-computes Basic (40%), HRA (50% of Basic), Special Allowance from CTC
Employees are soft-deleted (is_active = false) to preserve payslip foreign key integrity
Employee directory is readable by all roles; salary details visible only to Admin and Payroll Officer
Employee can mark daily attendance via a clock-in button; idempotency enforced via UNIQUE(employee_id, date) DB constraint
Status assigned automatically: clock-in before 9:30 AM = Present; after 9:30 AM = Late; no record by EOD = Absent (computed at payrun time)
HR Officer can view all employee attendance in a paginated monitor table with date and status filters
Admin can override any attendance record; override writes to audit_logs with: actor ID, before value, after value, timestamp, and override note
Employee can view their own attendance in a monthly calendar view
Employee can apply for leave specifying: type (casual/sick/earned/unpaid), start date, end date, and reason
Leave request enters Pending state on creation; Payroll Officer can Approve or Reject with a mandatory reason string
On approval, system auto-decrements leave_balances.consumed by total leave days for the applicable leave type
HR Officer can allocate annual leave quota per employee and per leave type
System enforces: employee cannot apply for leave if consumed >= allocated for that leave type
Unpaid leave (approved) flags the employee's monthly payrun for LOP deduction
Payroll Officer triggers monthly payrun for a specified month/year; UNIQUE(month, year) prevents duplicate runs
Payrun engine reads: salary_structures, attendance records, and approved leave_requests for each employee in the period
Engine computes: Basic = 40% CTC/12; HRA = 50% Basic; Gross = Basic + HRA + Special Allowance; PF = 12% Basic; PT = Maharashtra slab; LOP = (Gross/22) x unpaid days; Net = Gross - PF - PT - LOP
Each employee receives a payslip record in the database; Payroll Officer and Admin can view all payslips for a payrun
Employee can view and download their own payslip as a PDF; PDF generated server-side via PDFKit
Admin dashboard displays stat cards: total employees, attendance rate, leave requests pending, last payrun net total
Monthly attendance bar chart (Present/Absent/Late breakdown) rendered via Recharts with live DB data
Leave type distribution pie chart (Casual/Sick/Earned/Unpaid) for current month
Payroll trend line chart showing net pay total per month for the last 6 months
Employee personal dashboard shows: own attendance summary, leave balance by type, latest payslip net amount
95th percentile < 500ms for standard queries; payrun computation < 5s for 50 employees
